
### basic flooding 


* idea: broadcast message to whole network
* where message comes from = way to send back 
<hr class="vspace" />
* used this idea in MAC learning


### flooding in MAC learning



::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding-one-entry.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="A network with three switches connecting 6 hosts. Each switch has a neighbor table with destination MAC address and port columns."}

![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding-one-entry.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Host with MAC ending :AA sends a frame through the rightmost switch's port 1, which causes the rightmost switch to add an ':AA', port 1 entry to its neighbor table."}

![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding-one-entry.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="The frame sent by :AA is forwarded from the rightmost switch's port 4 to the top-left switch's port 1, causing the top-left switch to add an entry for :AA, port 1 to its own neighbor table."}

![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding-one-entry.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt="The frame sent by :AA is further forwarded from the top-left switch's port 5 to the bottom-left switch's port 2, causing the bottom-left switch to add its own entry for :AA, port 2 to its neighbor table."}


:::


### flooding IP routes



::: {.r-stack style="margin-top: -2.5em"}
 
![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 width=950px fig-alt="A network diagram with four routers (upper-left, lower-left, upper-right, lower-right), their routing tables, and their IP address (one for each network they are connected to). There are five networks in total, with IP ranges like 2001:db8:1::/40, 2001:db8:2::/40, etc.. Three of them only one router is connected to. The other two networks connect the routers: the right and lower-left routers are connected together, and the two left routers are connected together. Initially, the routers only have routing table entries for directly connected networks."}

![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 width=950px fig-alt="The lower-right router was initially missing a routing table entry for a network it is conencted to. It adds one (2001:db8:4::/40 via port 1, no gateway)."}

![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 width=950px fig-alt="After adding a routing table entry for its port 1, the lower-right router tells the routers that are the other network it is connected to about it. The message indicates that there is a route via 2001:db:2::3 (the lower right router's IP address on the shared network) to 2001:db8:4::/40 (the new route the lower-right router discovered)."}

![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 width=950px fig-alt="Receiving this message, the upper-right and lower-left routers add the route to their routing table: 2001:db8:4::/40 via 2001:db:2::3 (lower-right router). Each routing table entry also includes the port the routers use to access the network to which the lower-right router is connected."}

![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding.figure-5.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=5 width=950px fig-alt="The lower-left router further forwards its new information to the upper-left router. As a result, the upper-left router adds a new route for 2001:db8:4::/40 (the network from the lower-right router) via 2001:db8:f::2 (the lower-left router's IP address on the network connecting the two left rotuers)."}

![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding.figure-6.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=6 width=950px fig-alt="The upper-left router similarly floods its information about the 2001:db8:1::/40 network it is connected to. First it sends a message to the lower-left router, causing the lower-left router to add entry for 2001:db8:1::/40 with a gateway of 2001:db8:f::1 (the upper-left router's IP on the network it shares with the lower-left router)."}

![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding.figure-7.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=7 width=950px fig-alt="The lower-left router forwards its routing information to the right routers. As a result the two right routers add routes for both the 2001:db8:f::/40 network that connects the left routers and the 2001:db8:1:: that only the upper-left router is connected to. Both of these routes specify a gateway of the lower-left router's IP address on the network it shares with the right routers."} 

![](/routing-intro/texfig/flooding.figure-8.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=8 width=950px fig-alt="More sharing of routing inforemation between neighbors fills in additiona routing table entries, resulting in every router have routers for all five of the networks the routers are connected to."} 

:::


### eventual convergence  {.smaller}


* ‘flooding’ algorithm:
* periodically send on each network: 

   * list of routes you have that don't double-back to same network

* when receiving routes sent on network: 

   * add routing table entry for each route

### only one path? 


* only one path on network means: 
<hr class="vspace" />
* if a link fails, bad news
* network forms a tree


### routing like this?  {.smaller}


* for IP routing, generally want to have multiple paths
